selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Spend a full day hopping between the stunning Phi Phi islands by speedboat, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Monkey Beach, and swimming in vibrant coral reefs. Lunch is typically included on the boat.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene with a guided evening walk through bustling night markets. Sample pad thai, mango sticky rice, som tum, grilled satay, and fresh coconut ice cream from local vendors and hawker stalls.

experiences.name: Railay Beach Rock Climbing & Sunset Swim
experiences.description: Accessible only by longtail boat, Railay Beach offers dramatic limestone karst cliffs perfect for beginner rock climbing with a guide, followed by a relaxing swim and sunset views on one of Thailand's most secluded and picturesque beaches.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Kayaking & Mangrove Exploration
experiences.description: Paddle through serene mangrove forests and hidden sea caves around Koh Lanta on a guided kayaking tour. Discover local fishing villages, spot wildlife, and end the adventure relaxing on a quiet white-sand beach with turquoise waters.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Street Food & Night Bazaar Experience
experiences.description: Explore Chiang Mai's famous Saturday or Sunday Walking Street and Night Bazaar, tasting northern Thai specialties like khao soi (coconut curry noodles), sai oua (herbed sausage), and crispy pork rinds while browsing handmade crafts and soaking in local culture.
experiences.location: Wualai Road & Night Bazaar, Chiang Mai

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport, clear customs, and take a shared minivan or bus to the Rassada Pier in Phuket or Krabi Pier. Purchase a ferry ticket to Phi Phi Islands (budget tip: take the slow ferry for ~200-300 THB instead of a speedboat). Enjoy the scenic sea crossing and settle into your boutique stay on Phi Phi Don.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Tonsai Village — the main hub of Phi Phi Don. Explore the lively walking street, grab a cold Chang beer from a convenience store, and soak in the island atmosphere. Watch the sunset from the beachfront if energy allows.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during transit — grab a simple Thai rice porridge (khao tom) or a 7-Eleven snack for under 60 THB
meals.lunch: Pack a snack or buy from a pier food stall — pad kra pao (basil stir-fry) rice box for ~60-80 THB
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village street food stalls — try a pad thai or green curry with rice from a local vendor for 80-120 THB

day_by_day.notes: October is the tail end of the monsoon season on the Andaman side. Ferry schedules may be affected by weather — always check conditions at the pier. Book accommodation in advance as Phi Phi can fill up quickly. Keep 200-300 THB in cash for the ferry and small tips.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (Koh Phi Phi Don Viewpoint). The hike takes about 20-30 minutes and costs 30 THB entry. The panoramic view of the twin bays at sunrise is absolutely stunning and completely worth the effort. Bring water and wear good shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Long Beach on the southern tip of Phi Phi Don — a quieter and less crowded alternative to Tonsai Beach. Swim, snorkel, and relax. Rent a snorkel set from a beach shack for around 100 THB. The coral reefs here are accessible directly from the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village for dinner and explore the famous Phi Phi night market. Watch fire shows on the beach — they happen nightly for free and are a signature Phi Phi experience. Grab a fruit shake from a street stall.

meals.breakfast: Small guesthouse or local café near Tonsai — toast with eggs and coffee for 80-100 THB, or grab fresh fruit from a morning market cart
meals.lunch: Beach shack on Long Beach — grilled fish with sticky rice and a coconut for ~150 THB
meals.dinner: Night market in Tonsai Village — mix of grilled skewers, mango sticky rice, and fried spring rolls for under 150 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Start the viewpoint hike before 7:00 AM to avoid heat and crowds. Bring insect repellent for the jungle trail. Long Beach can be reached by a 10-minute walk or a short longtail boat ride (50 THB each way) from Tonsai Pier.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget group snorkeling day trip around Phi Phi Leh and nearby islands. Look for shared longtail boat tours departing from Tonsai Pier for around 400-600 THB per person. Stops typically include Maya Bay (of The Beach fame), Pileh Lagoon, Viking Cave, and Monkey Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour. Swim and snorkel at Pileh Lagoon — a sheltered emerald green lagoon surrounded by limestone cliffs. This is one of the most photogenic spots in all of Thailand. Snorkel gear is usually included in the tour price.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Rest and freshen up, then head out for a leisurely evening walk along the beach. Enjoy the golden hour light on the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or 7-Eleven near your guesthouse — banana roti or a Thai-style sandwich for 50-80 THB
meals.lunch: Packed lunch often included in group tours, or buy from a floating vendor at the island stops — budget 100-150 THB if not included
meals.dinner: Sit-down local restaurant in Tonsai — massaman curry with jasmine rice for 120-150 THB

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted access and specific visiting hours to protect coral restoration — confirm current rules with your tour operator before booking. Always apply reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine ecosystem. Negotiate group tour prices at the pier for better deals, especially if traveling with others.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (approximately 1.5-2 hours, ~200-250 THB). Arrive in Krabi Town and check out the famous Krabi Town Walking Street Market if it's a weekend, or explore the riverside promenade along the Krabi River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Kaew Korawaram — a stunning white Buddhist temple in the center of Krabi Town, free to enter. Then head to the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking panoramic views of Krabi Province. Entry is free but bring water and wear modest clothing.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's famous night market (Maharaj Road Walking Street on weekends or the daily evening market near the waterfront). Sample a wide variety of Thai street food at rock-bottom prices.

meals.breakfast: Eat before the ferry or grab something at the Phi Phi pier — roti with condensed milk for 40-60 THB
meals.lunch: Krabi Town local restaurant — khao man gai (poached chicken rice) for 60-80 THB
meals.dinner: Krabi Town night market — pad see ew, som tam, grilled pork skewers, and fresh coconut for under 200 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Store your luggage at your Phi Phi accommodation or at the ferry pier in Krabi (small fee applies) if you're doing a day trip. The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — go in the late afternoon to avoid the midday heat. Wear shoes with grip. Budget accommodation in Krabi Town starts from 300-500 THB per night if you decide to stay over.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Krabi Town or Ao Nang to the famous Four Islands (Si Island) tour — a budget island-hopping experience covering Koh Poda, Koh Gai (Chicken Island), Koh Tup, and Koh Mor. Group tours cost around 500-700 THB including snorkeling gear and lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands tour. At low tide, a sandbar emerges connecting Koh Tup and Koh Mor — a magical natural phenomenon perfect for photos. Snorkel around Koh Poda's coral garden and spot colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang Beach by late afternoon. Walk along Ao Nang's beachfront promenade, browse the souvenir shops for budget gifts, and enjoy the sunset over the iconic limestone karsts rising from the sea.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse or local café in Krabi Town — khao tom (rice porridge) with a soft-boiled egg for 60-80 THB
meals.lunch: Usually included in the Four Islands tour — simple beach BBQ or packed Thai lunch
meals.dinner: Ao Nang street food area — green papaya salad, grilled squid, and sticky rice for 150-180 THB

day_by_day.notes: Ao Nang is about 20 minutes from Krabi Town by songthaew (shared red truck taxi) for about 50 THB per person. Book the Four Islands tour at any guesthouse or travel agent the evening before for the best price. October weather may cause some tours to be cancelled — always have a backup plan.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (15-20 minutes, ~100 THB each way) — one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches, only accessible by boat due to towering limestone cliffs. Explore Railay West Beach and Railay East Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through the jungle trail to Phra Nang Cave Beach — one of the most stunning beaches in Southeast Asia, with a sacred princess cave shrine. Then attempt the short but steep hike to Railay Viewpoint for incredible aerial views of the peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Linger on Railay Beach for the sunset, then take the longtail back to Ao Nang. Spend the evening at a local restaurant or food stall in Ao Nang.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang local café — American breakfast with eggs, toast, and coffee for 100-120 THB
meals.lunch: Beachside food shack on Railay East — pad thai or fried rice for 120-150 THB (slightly more expensive due to location)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang walking street — tom kha soup with rice and a fruit smoothie for 150-180 THB

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach has no ATMs — bring enough cash before you go. The longtail boats operate until around 9:00 PM. Phra Nang Cave is considered sacred — be respectful of the shrine. The viewpoint hike involves rope-climbing sections and can be muddy in October — wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry or speedboat from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 2 hours, ~350-450 THB). Arrive and check in to a budget bungalow or hostel on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — one of Koh Lanta's most popular and beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and explore Long Beach — a wide, golden sandy beach with calm waters perfect for swimming. Rent a bicycle or motorbike (150-200 THB/day) to explore the island at your own pace. Visit the Old Town (Ban Ko Lanta) — a charming sea-gypsy fishing village with wooden shophouses on stilts over the water.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the west coast of Koh Lanta — some of the best sunsets in Thailand happen here. Head to a beachfront bar for a cheap happy-hour drink (beer from 60-80 THB) and enjoy the colors over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your Ao Nang guesthouse or grab something at the ferry pier before departure
meals.lunch: Old Town restaurant in Ban Ko Lanta — fresh seafood curry with rice for 120-150 THB
meals.dinner: Beach BBQ restaurant on Long Beach — grilled fish, morning glory stir-fry, and jasmine rice for 180-220 THB

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta ferries run seasonally — confirm schedules in advance as October is low season and some routes may have limited departures. The island is much quieter and more laid-back than Phi Phi, making it a perfect mid-trip recharge stop. Motorbike rental is the most efficient way to explore Koh Lanta's 30km length.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike and head to Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island (entry fee: 200 THB for foreigners). Hike to the lighthouse for spectacular views over the Andaman Sea and neighboring islands. Explore the park's beaches and jungle trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Klong Nin Beach — a quieter, more secluded beach on Koh Lanta's west coast. Snorkel in the clear waters or simply relax in a hammock at a beachside café. Stop by Kantiang Bay — a stunning crescent-shaped bay often considered Koh Lanta's most beautiful beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach for the evening. Visit the local market near the main road for cheap street food, or cook your own meal if your accommodation has a kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse café — banana pancake and fresh fruit smoothie for 80-100 THB
meals.lunch: Beachside shack at Kantiang Bay — grilled prawns with garlic butter and rice for 150-180 THB
meals.dinner: Local village market near Long Beach — mixed street food including satay, spring rolls, and mango sticky rice for under 150 THB

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your motorbike with petrol before heading south — fuel stations become sparse near the national park. The road to the southern tip is winding and can be slippery in wet conditions — drive carefully. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and snorkel gear from your accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry from Koh Lanta to Koh Phi Phi or directly to Phuket (depending on ferry availability in October). Head to Phuket Town — the cultural heart of Phuket, very different from the touristy beach areas. Check into a budget hostel in the Old Town area (dorms from 250-350 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-recognized area of beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture. Walk along Thalang Road, Dibuk Road, and Soi Rommanee (the most colorful street). Visit the weekend market or browse local art galleries and boutique coffee shops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the famous Sunday Walking Street Market in Phuket Old Town (if it's a Sunday) or the Indy Market on weekends. Otherwise, head to the local fresh market near Ranong Road for the most authentic and cheapest street food in Phuket.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during the ferry journey — pack snacks or buy from the ferry pier
meals.lunch: Phuket Town local restaurant — Phuket-style hokkien noodles (mee hokkien) for 60-80 THB
meals.dinner: Phuket Old Town walking street or local market — Phuket-style satay, oh tao (oyster pancake), and fresh coconut for under 200 THB

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Town is significantly cheaper than Patong or Kata beaches and offers a much more authentic Thai experience. The Old Town is walkable and very safe. Budget accommodation here is excellent value. Try the local Phuket specialty — moo hong (braised pork belly) — at a traditional kopitiam coffee shop.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local songthaew (40-50 THB) from Phuket Town to Kata Beach or Karon Beach — two of Phuket's best beaches that are less crowded and cheaper than Patong. Swim and enjoy the beach in the morning when it's least crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short songthaew to Kata Noi Beach — a smaller, more secluded cove just south of Kata. Then hike up to the Kata Viewpoint (free) for stunning panoramic views over Kata, Kata Noi, and Karon beaches — one of the most photographed views in Phuket.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Phuket Town for dinner. Visit the Phuket Weekend Night Market (Naka Market) if available, or explore the local evening food scene around Ranong Road wet market area.

meals.breakfast: Old Town kopitiam — traditional Phuket coffee with condensed milk and kaya toast for 50-70 THB
meals.lunch: Beach food stall at Kata Beach — fried rice with egg and a fresh coconut for 100-130 THB
meals.dinner: Phuket Town local restaurant — gaeng som (sour curry) with rice and a Thai iced tea for 100-130 THB

day_by_day.notes: Songthaews from Phuket Town to Kata/Karon run regularly throughout the day but may be infrequent in the evening — plan your return trip accordingly. October can bring large swells to Phuket's west coast beaches — always check the red/yellow flag system before swimming. Never swim when red flags are flying.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Phi Phi Islands from Phuket via a budget group speedboat tour (600-900 THB including snorkeling) — or alternatively, join a budget tour to James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan) in Phang Nga Bay (500-700 THB by shared longtail). The Phang Nga Bay tour is one of Thailand's most dramatic landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour — paddle through mangrove forests by kayak (often included or available as an add-on for 200-300 THB), explore sea caves, and visit the Muslim fishing village of Koh Panyee built entirely on stilts over the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket Town by late afternoon. Spend the evening exploring the Old Town's bar scene — many bars offer cheap happy hours with local beer from 60-80 THB. Try a Singha or Leo beer at a rooftop bar overlooking the Sino-Portuguese buildings.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite at a local bakery or 7-Eleven before the morning tour departure — 50-80 THB
meals.lunch: Usually included in Phang Nga Bay tours — simple Thai lunch at Koh Panyee floating village restaurant
meals.dinner: Phuket Old Town — khao pad sapparod (pineapple fried rice served in a pineapple) for 150-180 THB at a local restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book the Phang Nga Bay tour the evening before from any travel agent in Phuket Town — prices are negotiable especially in low season. The floating village at Koh Panyee has a football pitch built on stilts — one of the most unique sports venues in the world. Bring a light rain jacket as October afternoons can bring sudden showers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Big Buddha of Phuket (Phra Phrom Maha Wihan) — a massive 45-meter white marble Buddha statue on top of Nakkerd Hill. Entry is free. Take a local songthaew or rent a motorbike to get there. The views over Phuket, Kata, and Karon are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Rawai Beach in southern Phuket — a local fishing beach with a famous seafood market. Buy fresh seafood directly from the vendors at the market (per kilogram prices) and have it cooked at one of the adjacent restaurants for a small cooking fee. This is one of the cheapest and freshest seafood experiences in Phuket.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Promthep Cape — the southernmost tip of Phuket — for the most famous sunset viewpoint on the island. Arrive 30-45 minutes before sunset to get a good spot. Afterward, head back to Phuket Town for a final evening of street food exploration.

meals.breakfast: Old Town café — fresh fruit platter and Thai-style coffee for 80-100 THB
meals.lunch: Rawai seafood market — buy fresh prawns, squid, and fish and have them grilled at a market restaurant for 200-300 THB total (excellent value for fresh seafood)
meals.dinner: Final night street food feast in Phuket Town — try everything you haven't tried yet: oyster omelette, grilled corn, mango with sticky rice, and fresh coconut ice cream for under 200 THB

day_by_day.notes: The Big Buddha is a sacred site — dress modestly (cover shoulders and knees). Sarongs are available to borrow at the entrance. Promthep Cape gets very crowded at sunset — arrive early. The Rawai seafood market is best visited at lunchtime when the catch is freshest. Bargain politely for the best prices on seafood.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final morning in Phuket. Visit a local fresh market for breakfast — try khao niao mamuang (mango sticky rice) or pa thong ko (Thai donuts) with warm soy milk. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the Old Town — local handicrafts, Thai spices, and silk items are great budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head to the airport or squeeze in one final activity — a visit to Wat Chalong, Phuket's most important Buddhist temple (free entry), located about 15 minutes south of Phuket Town by songthaew.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Phuket International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of island hopping, beach adventures, and unforgettable street food across Thailand's stunning Andaman Coast.

meals.breakfast: Local fresh market near Phuket Town — khao niao mamuang and Thai donuts with soy milk for 60-80 THB
meals.lunch: Airport food court — pad thai or fried rice for 120-150 THB (slightly more expensive than town but still reasonable)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight — grab a final Thai snack before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for Phuket Airport check-in, especially during busy periods. Keep some Thai baht for airport transport and any last purchases. The AOT limousine or shared minivan from Phuket Town to the airport costs 150-200 THB per person. Don't forget to declare any food items when returning home. Average daily budget for this trip: approximately 800-1,200 THB (USD 22-34) per day excluding accommodation and transport between islands.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and collect luggage. Take a shared minivan or private transfer to Rassada Pier in Phuket Town, then board a high-speed ferry to Phi Phi Don Island (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Bay to get your bearings and soak in the island atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village walking street. Browse local shops, watch fire shows on the beach, and settle into the relaxed Phi Phi vibe.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or meal at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the pier or on the ferry — pack a sandwich or buy from pier-side stalls
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant on Tonsai Bay — affordable Thai classics like pad thai, green curry, and fresh seafood platters in a casual beachside setting

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance during October as it is shoulder season and boats can fill up. Carry some Thai Baht cash for the ferry and tips. October can bring occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise hike up to Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–40 min climb). The panoramic view over the twin bays of Phi Phi Don is spectacular and best enjoyed before the midday heat. Bring water and wear good footwear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling longtail boat tour around Phi Phi's iconic spots: Monkey Beach, Viking Cave, and the crystal-clear waters of Loh Samah Bay. Snorkel gear is usually included in tour packages (approx. 400–600 THB per person).
day_by_day.evening: Relax on Loh Dalum Beach as the sun sets. Watch the famous fire show performers on the beach and enjoy the lively but laid-back night scene.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — try a Thai-style breakfast with rice congee (jok) and iced coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or grab fresh fruit and snacks from Tonsai market stalls before the boat tour
meals.dinner: Unni's Restaurant — a beloved Phi Phi institution serving excellent Thai and Western fusion dishes at mid-range prices; try the massaman curry

day_by_day.notes: Start the viewpoint hike by 6:00–6:30 AM for the best light and cooler temperatures. Apply sunscreen generously before the snorkeling tour. Bring a dry bag for your electronics on the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day island hopping tour departing from Tonsai Pier. Morning stop at Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh — the iconic lagoon made famous by the film 'The Beach.' Arrive early to beat the crowds. Swim in the turquoise waters and explore the surrounding limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island hopping tour to Pileh Lagoon (a stunning enclosed emerald lagoon), Shark Point for snorkeling with black-tip reef sharks, and Bamboo Island with its white sandy beach for a relaxed lunch stop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Shower and unwind. Head out for a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking Tonsai Bay.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the tour departs (usually around 8:00–8:30 AM)
meals.lunch: Beachside BBQ lunch included in most full-day island hopping packages, typically served at Bamboo Island
meals.dinner: Cosmic Restaurant — great atmosphere with Thai street food-style dishes; try the pad kra pao (Thai basil stir-fry) and mango sticky rice for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the Maya Bay tour through a reputable operator to ensure they follow environmental guidelines. Maya Bay has visitor caps and timed entry — confirm your tour includes a confirmed slot. Wear reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning longtail boat to the quieter east side of Phi Phi Don — visit Laem Tong Beach, a more secluded stretch of white sand popular with snorkelers. Explore the shallow reef just off the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tonsai and spend the afternoon taking a beginner's PADI Discover Scuba Diving experience or a Freediving intro course (several reputable dive schools operate on the island, approx. 2,500–3,500 THB). Alternatively, rent a kayak and paddle around the bay at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening — browse the night market stalls near the pier for souvenirs and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Local Thai breakfast spot near the hotel — try khanom krok (coconut pancakes) and fresh-cut tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Beachside shack at Laem Tong Beach — fresh grilled fish and som tam (green papaya salad)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Tonsai Village walking street — grilled satay skewers, spring rolls, and pad see ew from various stalls (budget-friendly and delicious)

day_by_day.notes: Laem Tong is about 20–30 minutes by longtail from Tonsai; negotiate the price before boarding (approx. 400–600 THB round trip for a shared boat). October waters are generally calm on the east side of the island.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi by morning ferry to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hrs). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel in Krabi Town or Ao Nang. Drop your bags and head to the famous Krabi Town Floating Market (open Thursday–Sunday) for local snacks and handmade goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking 360-degree views over Krabi's karst landscape. The climb takes about 30–45 minutes and is strenuous but very rewarding.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Krabi Town's riverside night market (Chao Fa Pier Walking Street) — one of the best street food scenes in southern Thailand.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel or a bakery café in Tonsai before the ferry
meals.lunch: Floating Market in Krabi Town — try boat noodles, grilled corn, and fresh coconut ice cream
meals.dinner: Krabi Town Night Market at Chao Fa Pier — feast on grilled seafood, roti with banana and condensed milk, and fresh-squeezed juices for very reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is best done in the late afternoon (after 4:00 PM) to avoid peak heat. Wear modest clothing as it is a Buddhist temple. Bring plenty of water. Confirm your accommodation in Krabi Town or Ao Nang is booked ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Join a Four Islands boat tour departing from Ao Nang or Krabi Town pier. Visit Koh Mor, Koh Chuak, Koh Mah, and Koh Kwang — a mix of snorkeling reefs, sandy beaches, and a lagoon accessible only at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon free time at Tup Island (Koh Tup) — a stunning sandbar that connects two islands at low tide, perfect for photos and wading in shallow turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang. Explore Ao Nang Beach at sunset — enjoy a cold drink at one of the beachfront bars as the sun dips behind the limestone cliffs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local coffee shop near Ao Nang — try Thai-style toast with pandan jam and kopi (Thai coffee)
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch included in most Four Islands tour packages — typically a simple Thai set meal on one of the islands
meals.dinner: Ao Nang Walking Street — wide selection of mid-range restaurants; try Carnivore Steak & Grill for a treat or Last Fisherman Bar for fresh seafood with great sea views

day_by_day.notes: The Four Islands tour costs approximately 500–800 THB per person from Ao Nang. Check tide times as Tup Island sandbar is only accessible at low tide. October can have afternoon rain — tours usually still run but check with operators on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (15–20 min, approx. 100 THB each way) — accessible only by boat due to surrounding cliffs. Explore Railay West Beach and Railay East Beach, and hike to Phra Nang Cave Beach, one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try rock climbing on Railay's world-famous limestone cliffs — several schools offer beginner half-day sessions (approx. 800–1,200 THB). Alternatively, kayak around the headland to explore hidden lagoons and sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Railay West Beach before catching the last longtail back to Ao Nang. Enjoy a quiet evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Café near Ao Nang pier — smoothie bowl or eggs and toast before the boat
meals.lunch: Railay Beach restaurant strip — try the fresh seafood BBQ platters or green curry at one of the mid-range beachside spots
meals.dinner: Ao Nang — Lae Lay Grill restaurant for romantic seaside dining with Thai seafood specialties (slightly splurge-worthy for a special evening)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is very popular — arrive early to enjoy Phra Nang Cave Beach before the crowds. The cave shrine on the beach is sacred to local fishermen; be respectful. Longtail boats run until approximately 6:00–7:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry or minivan+ferry combination (approx. 2–2.5 hrs, 350–500 THB). Check into a mid-range bungalow resort on Long Beach (Klong Dao) or Klong Nin Beach — Koh Lanta's most beautiful stretches of sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (approx. 200–300 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta Old Town on the east coast — a charming stilted fishing village with wooden shophouses, local cafés, and a relaxed old-world atmosphere. Visit the Lanta Old Town pier and browse artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the southern tip of the island to watch the sunset from Mu Ko Lanta National Park viewpoint — stunning views over the Andaman Sea.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure in Krabi — pick up something at a convenience store or local stall near the pier
meals.lunch: Koh Lanta Old Town — try the local Muslim-style cuisine at one of the wooden shophouse restaurants; roti with curry is a must
meals.dinner: Somewhere Else Restaurant on Long Beach — excellent Thai dishes and fresh seafood in a beachside setting with fire torches and a relaxed vibe

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is significantly quieter than Phi Phi and Krabi — perfect for a mid-trip reset. Scooter rental is the best way to explore the 30km-long island. Drive carefully on the roads as some sections are narrow and winding. October is still considered low season for Lanta — some restaurants may be closed; ask your hotel for current recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day snorkeling trip to the Koh Haa (Five Islands) archipelago — one of the best snorkeling and diving sites in the Andaman Sea, with crystal-clear visibility, vibrant coral gardens, and sea turtles. Tours depart from Ban Saladan Pier (approx. 1,200–1,800 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snorkeling at Koh Rok — a stunning uninhabited island with pristine white sand and some of the clearest water in Thailand. Relax on the beach during the surface interval.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta. Shower and head to the beach for a relaxed evening. Catch a live acoustic music session at one of the beachfront bars on Long Beach.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a smoothie and toast at a beachside café before the tour
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the Koh Haa/Koh Rok tour — typically a Thai set meal served on board or on the beach
meals.dinner: Time for Lime Restaurant — a well-known cooking school and restaurant on Koh Lanta; excellent fresh Thai cuisine with a portion of proceeds supporting local community projects

day_by_day.notes: Koh Haa and Koh Rok are protected marine parks — entry fees apply (approx. 400 THB). Book through a licensed eco-conscious operator. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a rash guard, and an underwater camera if you have one.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at leisure on Klong Nin Beach — one of Koh Lanta's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches. Read, swim, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. Alternatively, book a morning yoga class (several resorts offer drop-in sessions for approx. 300–400 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Khlong Chak Waterfall in the southern part of the island (accessible by scooter, then a 30-min jungle trek). Cool off in the natural pool at the base of the falls. Explore the mangrove canal by kayak nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Klong Dao Beach for sunset — a long, gentle beach perfect for a golden-hour walk. Enjoy a final Koh Lanta evening with cocktails and fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Beachside breakfast at your resort or a local warung — try fresh fruit platters, granola, and Thai iced tea
meals.lunch: Simple local restaurant near Khlong Chak — grilled chicken with rice (khao man gai) or noodle soup
meals.dinner: Drunken Sailors Bar & Restaurant on Klong Dao Beach — popular with travelers, great cocktails, and solid Thai and Western menu options at mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: The waterfall trek can be muddy in October — wear sandals or shoes you don't mind getting wet. The mangrove kayaking is best done in the late afternoon when the light is golden. This is a good day to do laundry at a local laundry service (very affordable in Thailand).

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Koh Lanta back to Krabi, then connect via minivan transfer to Phuket (total journey approx. 3–4 hrs). Check into a mid-range hotel in Phuket — Old Town area recommended for character and convenience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town on foot — a beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese heritage district with colorful shophouses, street art murals, temples, and independent cafés. Visit Thalang Road, Soi Romanee (the most photogenic alley), and the Blue Elephant Cooking School building.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Sunday Walking Street Market if it's a Sunday, or the Saturday Night Market at Phuket Town (Indy Market) — two of Thailand's best night markets for street food and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure from Koh Lanta — hotel breakfast or grab-and-go from a local stall
meals.lunch: Phuket Old Town — try the famous Phuket-style dim sum (tim sum) or khao tom (rice porridge) at one of the heritage shophouse restaurants
meals.dinner: Phuket Night Market — an incredible spread of local Phuket specialties: mee hokkien (Hokkien noodles), o-tao (oyster cake), and Phuket lobster satay

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. Many of the heritage buildings have been converted into boutique hotels, galleries, and cafés. The Old Town area is much more authentic and affordable than the beach resort areas. Book your hotel in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phang Nga Bay — one of Thailand's most dramatic landscapes. Join a sea kayaking tour through towering limestone karsts, hidden hongs (sea caves accessible only by kayak), and mangrove tunnels. James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan) is a highlight of most tours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Phang Nga Bay — visit a Muslim fishing village built on stilts over the water at Koh Panyi. Browse local seafood restaurants and souvenir stalls. Return to Phuket by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Phuket — watch the sunset from Promthep Cape at the southern tip of the island (one of Thailand's most famous sunset viewpoints). Then head to Chalong or Rawai for a farewell seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phuket before the early departure for Phang Nga Bay
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Koh Panyi floating village — fresh grilled fish, crab curry, and cold drinks with a view over the bay
meals.dinner: Kan Eang@Pier Restaurant in Chalong — a Phuket institution for fresh seafood dining on the waterfront; try the steamed fish with lime and garlic and the tiger prawns

day_by_day.notes: Book the Phang Nga Bay sea kayaking tour through a reputable operator (approx. 1,200–1,800 THB). John Gray's Sea Canoe is the original and most eco-conscious operator. Arrive at Promthep Cape at least 30 minutes before sunset to secure a good viewing spot — it gets crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — if your flight allows, take a sunrise walk along Patong, Kata, or Karon Beach. Visit a local fresh market for one last taste of Thai street food: fresh fruit, rotis, and Thai iced coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, either relax at your hotel pool or do some last-minute souvenir shopping in Phuket Old Town. Pick up Thai tea, dried mango, coconut snacks, and local handicrafts to bring home. Head to Phuket International Airport with ample time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 13 incredible days in Thailand's islands, beaches, and street food scenes.

meals.breakfast: One last Thai breakfast — khao tom (rice porridge with ginger and egg) at a local market stall or hotel café
meals.lunch: Airport food court or a final street food stop near the hotel — pad thai or a green curry for the road
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Phuket International Airport. Keep some Thai Baht for airport snacks and last-minute purchases. Double-check that all souvenirs comply with customs regulations — dried fruits and sealed packaged foods are generally fine. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Rassada Pier in Phuket, followed by a luxury speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 45–60 min). Check in to your boutique stay, unwind on your private terrace, and take a leisurely stroll along Tonsai Bay to soak in the island atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking the Andaman Sea, followed by a relaxed first dinner at the resort or a top-rated beachfront restaurant on Phi Phi Don.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light bites at the airport lounge or grab-and-go snacks during transfer
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant or Blanco Beach Bar — fresh seafood, Thai classics, and craft cocktails in a premium beachfront setting

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your private speedboat transfer in advance through your boutique stay. October can bring occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket. Keep the evening low-key to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged by your boutique stay. Follow with a guided snorkeling excursion to the famous Maya Bay (The Beach) before the day-trippers arrive — crystal-clear waters and vibrant coral reefs await.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private longtail boat island-hopping tour visiting Pileh Lagoon, Viking Cave, and Loh Samah Bay. Swim, snorkel, and photograph the dramatic limestone karsts. Return to the resort for a refreshing outdoor shower and poolside relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Tonsai Village's vibrant night market for street food sampling — pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, and fresh coconut ice cream. End the night with a fire show performance on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Full Thai breakfast at your boutique stay — congee, fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and Thai tea
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood BBQ lunch on a secluded beach stop during the island-hopping tour
meals.dinner: Street food crawl through Tonsai Village Night Market — budget ฿500–800 per person for a premium street food experience

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Maya Bay tour for early morning (6:30–7:00 AM departure) to avoid crowds. Maya Bay has restricted visitor numbers — confirm access with your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Hike to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 min ascent) for panoramic views over both bays of Koh Phi Phi Don — one of Thailand's most iconic vistas. Best experienced at sunrise or mid-morning before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private half-day scuba diving experience at top dive sites around Phi Phi — Hin Phae, Bida Nok, and Bida Nai offer exceptional visibility and marine biodiversity including leopard sharks and sea turtles. Certified dives or a Discover Scuba session for beginners.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic beachfront dinner under the stars at a premium restaurant on Long Beach, known for its quieter, more upscale atmosphere compared to Tonsai.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh smoothie bowl and pastries from a café near Tonsai Pier before the hike
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café on Long Beach post-diving — fresh spring rolls, green papaya salad, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Cove Phi Phi or a comparable premium beachfront venue — grilled tiger prawns, massaman curry, and local craft beer or wine

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy footwear for the viewpoint hike — the trail is steep and can be slippery after rain. Book diving with a PADI 5-star dive center for the best safety and equipment standards.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private speedboat excursion departing from Phi Phi to the Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) — a pristine, less-visited island with powder-white sand and turquoise waters. Snorkeling, swimming, and beachcombing in near-total seclusion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping route to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for exceptional snorkeling among colorful reef fish, then anchor near Phi Phi Leh for a late-afternoon swim in Pileh Lagoon's emerald-green enclosed bay.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by sunset. Freshen up and enjoy a private in-villa dinner arranged by your boutique stay — a curated Thai tasting menu served on your terrace with sea views.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the resort — fresh croissants, local fruits, yogurt, and pressed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by your resort and enjoyed on Bamboo Island's beach
meals.dinner: Private in-villa Thai tasting menu — tom kha gai, som tum, massaman lamb, and mango sorbet dessert (pre-arrange with hotel)

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day on-water experience — bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. October seas are generally calm but confirm weather conditions the morning of departure.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort — enjoy the pool, spa treatment (Thai massage or aromatherapy), or paddleboarding along the bay. A perfect slower-paced morning after several active days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer from Phi Phi Islands to Krabi Town (approx. 90 min). Check in to a luxury property in Krabi — such as Rayavadee or Sofitel Krabi Phokeethra — and explore the hotel grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's famous Chao Fah Weekend Night Market (or Maharaj Market on weekdays) for an authentic street food experience — pad see ew, roti with condensed milk, fresh oyster omelets, and tropical fruit.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Phi Phi boutique stay — full Thai spread with fresh-caught fish
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — stop at a riverside restaurant in Krabi Town for crab curry and river views
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Krabi Night Market — curated tasting of 6–8 dishes from different stalls, budget ฿600–1,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrange luggage transfer and speedboat in advance. Maharaj Market operates daily while Chao Fah is weekends — check the day of the week and plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning four-island tour by private longtail boat from Krabi, visiting Koh Mor, Koh Tub, Koh Chicken (Koh Kai), and Koh Poda — each offering unique snorkeling, sandbar walks, and dramatic karst scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Krabi and visit the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Seua) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for sweeping views over Krabi Province. Descend and visit the cave shrine at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a rooftop bar in Ao Nang, followed by a premium dinner at a top-rated Krabi restaurant featuring southern Thai cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — rice porridge, fried egg, Thai sausage, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch on Koh Poda beach — grilled fish, som tum, and sticky rice brought by your private boat crew
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ruen Mai Restaurant in Krabi Town — renowned for authentic southern Thai cuisine, fresh seafood, and local herbs (reserve in advance)

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is demanding — wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Best attempted in late afternoon when temperatures are cooler. The four-island tour is ideal in the morning for calmer seas.

day_by_day.morning: Private kayaking and mangrove tour through the Ao Thalane mangrove forest — paddle through sea caves, hidden lagoons, and lush green tunnels with a knowledgeable local guide. Spot monitor lizards, kingfishers, and mudskippers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing experience on the world-famous limestone karsts of Railay Beach — accessible only by longtail boat. Beginner to advanced routes with certified guides. Alternatively, relax on the stunning Railay West Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Longtail boat back to Ao Nang at golden hour. Private Thai cooking class at a premium culinary studio — learn to prepare 4–5 classic dishes including green curry, pad thai, and coconut soup.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs benedict with a Thai twist, fresh fruit platter, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Railay Beach — fresh seafood wrap, papaya salad, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Eat the dishes you cooked during the cooking class — a truly immersive culinary experience

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by longtail boat from Ao Nang (10–15 min). Book rock climbing with a reputable operator such as King Climbers for safety and quality instruction.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private speedboat charter to the Koh Lanta area — explore the beautiful beaches of Koh Lanta Yai, snorkel at Hin Daeng and Hin Muang (two of Thailand's top dive sites, known for manta ray sightings in season).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Koh Rok — a remote, protected marine park with some of the clearest water in the Andaman Sea. Snorkel among pristine coral gardens and tropical fish. Anchor for a peaceful afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return speedboat journey to Krabi at sunset — champagne on deck as the sun dips behind the limestone karsts. Quiet evening at the hotel with room service or the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast from the hotel — fresh baguette, cheese, and fruit to eat on the boat
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch on board — Thai-style bento boxes with rice, grilled chicken, and fresh fruit prepared by the hotel
meals.dinner: In-hotel dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — seafood platter, Thai red curry, and a premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is a national marine park — entry fees apply. Manta ray sightings at Hin Daeng/Hin Muang are more common November–April, but October can still yield sightings. Confirm with your dive operator.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in, enjoy a spa morning at the hotel (couple's massage, body scrub, or facial). Take a dip in the hotel pool and enjoy a late breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Krabi Airport for a short domestic flight to Chiang Mai (approx. 1.5–2 hrs). Alternatively, fly via Bangkok if no direct route is available. Check in to a luxury boutique resort in Chiang Mai's Old City or Nimman area.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introduction to Chiang Mai — evening walk through the Old City walls, visit Wat Chedi Luang temple illuminated at night, and explore the Sunday Night Walking Street (if applicable to the day) or Nimman Road's upscale bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Late luxurious breakfast at Krabi hotel — full buffet spread with made-to-order eggs and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or light bites during transit
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Chiang Mai at David's Kitchen or Huen Phen — northern Thai cuisine including khao soi, sai oua sausage, and nam prik noom dip

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flights well in advance. Consider flying Bangkok Airways or Thai Airways for a more premium domestic experience. Chiang Mai's Old City is compact and very walkable in the evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Doi Suthep Temple — Chiang Mai's most iconic landmark perched on a forested mountain. Arrive before 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Enjoy sweeping views over the city from the temple terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Elephant Nature Park or a reputable ethical elephant sanctuary — spend the afternoon feeding, bathing, and walking alongside rescued elephants in a responsible, no-riding environment. A deeply moving and premium experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and explore the Nimman area — Chiang Mai's trendy, upscale neighborhood filled with art galleries, specialty coffee shops, boutique stores, and rooftop bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Nimman café — acai bowls, single-origin pour-over coffee, and avocado toast at a specialty café like Ristr8to
meals.lunch: Lunch at the elephant sanctuary — a vegetarian Thai buffet is typically included in the sanctuary experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ginger & Kafe inside The House restaurant — elegant northern Thai cuisine in a beautifully restored heritage house

day_by_day.notes: Book the elephant sanctuary well in advance — reputable sanctuaries fill up quickly. Ensure you choose an ethical operator that does not offer elephant riding, shows, or painting. Doi Suthep requires a songthaew or private car — arrange through your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Premium street food tour of Chiang Mai's morning markets — visit Warorot Market (Kad Luang) and the surrounding lanes for northern Thai breakfast staples: khao tom (rice soup), pa thong ko (Thai donuts) with pandan custard, and fresh-squeezed juices. Guided by a local food expert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chiang Mai Arts and Cultural Centre and explore the Saturday/Sunday Walking Street (Wualai Road) for handcrafted silverware, silk, and local art. Alternatively, take a private Thai silk weaving or pottery class at a local artisan studio.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar with Old City views, followed by a premium dinner at one of Chiang Mai's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast tour — 8–10 tastings across Warorot Market and surrounds
meals.lunch: Northern Thai lunch at Huen Muan Jai — a beloved local restaurant serving authentic Lanna-style cuisine including gaeng hang lay (Burmese-influenced pork curry)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Blackitch Artisan Kitchen or 137 Pillars House — a refined tasting menu experience showcasing elevated Thai and fusion cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Warorot Market is most vibrant early morning (6:00–9:00 AM). Hire a local food guide through your hotel for the best insider experience. The Saturday Walking Street on Wualai Road is one of the best in Thailand.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient city of Chiang Rai by private car (3 hrs). Visit the extraordinary White Temple (Wat Rong Khun) — a contemporary masterpiece of Buddhist art — and the Blue Temple (Wat Rong Suea Ten) with its vibrant azure interiors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Black House (Baan Dam Museum) — a striking collection of dark, traditional structures filled with art and artifacts. Visit a local hill tribe village for a respectful cultural encounter and browse handmade crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chiang Mai by private car. Final evening in the north — enjoy a traditional Khantoke dinner, a ceremonial northern Thai feast served on a low tray accompanied by classical Lanna dance performances.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — congee, fresh fruit, and Thai tea
meals.lunch: Lunch in Chiang Rai at a riverside restaurant near the Night Bazaar area — fresh river fish, larb, and sticky rice
meals.dinner: Khantoke dinner experience at Old Chiang Mai Cultural Centre — a multi-course northern Thai feast with traditional dance (reserve in advance)

day_by_day.notes: The Chiang Rai day trip is long — depart by 7:30 AM to maximize time. Hire a knowledgeable private driver/guide for the full day. The White Temple is closed on Mondays — verify the day before booking.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — slow breakfast at a beloved Chiang Mai café. Last-minute shopping at the Nimman boutiques or a nearby artisan market for premium Thai silk, handcrafted jewelry, or specialty coffee beans to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Chiang Mai International Airport for your departure flight. Depart with unforgettable memories of Thailand's beaches, islands, and northern culture.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at transit hub — reflect on 13 extraordinary days across Thailand's finest destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast at a beloved local café — khao tom, fresh fruit, and specialty Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Airport lounge dining or a final quick bite of pad thai or mango sticky rice before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at layover destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Chiang Mai Airport. Pack any liquid items (sauces, coconut oil, etc.) in checked luggage. Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transfer the evening before.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
